The future holds for us many different possibilities. Endless enduring against the flow time. I sought nothing as my head gazed upon the sidewalk, blending perfectly well with the sea of people that surround me. It was not long before I stumbled upon a sign in the window of a large yellow building. I paused but for a moment to gaze upon the empty glass windows. Just a touch of dust covered shelves and empty displays, the carcass of what was once someone’s dream. I touch my fingers to the cool glass and slide my hand along as I begin to walk down the sidewalk once again.

The building was once my childhood home. I remember staring out the window on a hot summer day near the AC trying to get a blast of cool air before mother yelled to have me turn it off. My father sank everything he had into that store. It wasn't much but my father had a passion for reading, and stocked his shelves with the greatest book's he could find, determined to educate the town we lived in with both fiction and reality.

Alas, my father’s dream slowly faded into nothing. As we grew older the business began to decline. My father couldn't understand it and memories of watching people pass along the sidewalks was replaced with the worried stare of my father outside the store waiting for a customer to come. I remember a man who would spend his days reading all the book's in his store, waiting for the next customer to come in so that he can lead them to their next great adventure. Now his eyes have become dull, the excitement waned and the fear of losing it all seemed enviable.

The dawn of the computer age was my father’s downfall, and shortly after the turn of the century my father was forced to close down the shop and move us out of the home I knew my entire life. My parents began to argue, they fought day and night for my father had no formal college education, and my mother no working experience. Finding work was tough, and eventually my father began to drink.

It wasn't long after my father fell into a black hole of rum soaked depression that my mother left us. My father worked day and night at any job he could find to raise me into early manhood, and once I was able, I enlisted in the military to help my father with the household finances.

Now I find myself here, a well-trained Solider with a cocky attitude and two months of pay in my pocket. I was eager to see my father but as I approached the front steps to our new apartment, I knew something was wrong. I walked up the two flights of stairs and knocked heavily on the door with no response. I reached for my key and opened the door slowly, calling to my father. I began to panic and my heart began to freeze. My palms grew cold with sweat as I frantically searched the apartment.

Only after searching every room I found a note.

Dear Son,

I want you to always know how proud I am of you, and how I wish I could have made life better for us. It was never my intention to fail you or your mother and I hope you know that I couldn't bear the thought of putting you through what I had done. I am so proud of you for living up to the potential I always knew you had. Remember son that we cannot change the past, and we cannot predict the future. The only thing we can do accept that we are trapped within the current of time, and our destinations are unknown until we arrive. It is time for me to meet my destination son and while I longed to see you and embrace you once again, I could no longer keep with the burdens of my failure. You will find in the safe, the sum of everything I own. I hope it is enough to provide to you a good future.

Love always,

Dad

The letter dropped from my hands, and I fell too quickly into the seat behind me. I didn't cry, I didn't shed a tear, I just stared at the wall in front of me, thinking of all the possibilities that could have been other than this one. Why did it have to be this way? Why did he feel the need to do this? I find the strength to pick myself up and reach for my cell phone in my pocket. As I call the police I stare out the window of our apartment and for the first time noticed it overlooked the old store down the block. The old sign swinging in the wind, as if clinging to what little life it once used to have.

This was very powerful! It's poignant for me as I lost my dad a few years back. He tried so hard to provide for us while my siblings and I were growing up. There were times I think he might have given up if it hadn't been for us kids. This story made me think of him, and his struggle through the hard times.

Thank you.
